messages:
mina: heads-up — on the orion-v2 int4 bringup we’re seeing a BLEU drop on zh->ja when the source contains ruby/furigana and linewraps vertically. nightly eval shows ~3.9 BLEU delta. attaching quick repro below.

evalbot: nightly-run | orion-v2-int4 vs orion-v2-fp16 | dataset=zh_ja_ruby_v2 | BLEU: fp16=34.7, int4=30.8 (delta -3.9) | tests=1200 pairs | commit=a1b2c3d

chen_w: can you paste the minimal input and the exact eval command?

mina: sure — sample input (short):
```
今朝[振り仮名]{ruby:きょう}は晴れです。
```
eval command I used: `python eval/compare.py --model orion-v2-int4 --ref orion-v2-fp16 --dataset zh_ja_ruby_v2 --metrics bleu --linewrap vertical`

liam_dev: repro'd locally on a small subset. interestingly, when I run with `--linewrap horizontal` the gap shrinks to ~0.6. vertical wrapping triggers extra token merges around the ZWJ/furigana sequences.

sara_ml: hmm — could be tokenizer normalization + quant kernel ordering. did we change any tokenizer merges in the int4 tokenizer map for orion?

mina: not intentionally. but we did merge the new tokenmap patch two commits ago (tokenmap: 5f4e7). trying to rule out tokenmap vs kernel.

liam_dev: quick check: `tools/tokenmap-inspect --input sample.txt --model orion-v2-int4` shows different token ids between fp16 and int4 for the ruby bracket sequence. looks like the byte-level detokenization path is producing an extra merge token in int4 build.

chen_w: can you paste the token id sequences? even a tiny example helps.

mina: pasted below:
fp16 ids: [821, 3345, 1999, 44, 77]
int4 ids: [821, 3345, 1999, 1999, 44, 77]  <-- duplicate 1999 inserted

liam_dev: duplicate id explains shifted alignment -> BLEU penalty. sounds like an emission/merge regression in the quantized tokenizer encoder path or in the fast-kv decode.

sara_ml: Did the kernel selector change for small sequence pack? there was a recent fallback for short sequences to the packed-kernel that doesn't respect the pre-tokenized merge table. commit a1b2c3d looks suspicious.

mina: agree. I tried swapping back to the previous kernel (`--kernel fast-merge-v1`) at runtime and the int4 BLEU returns to within 0.2 of fp16 for the sample run.

chen_w: nice isolation. can you run a bisect across commits between 5f4e7..a1b2c3d? `git bisect run tests/eval_smoke.sh` should catch it.

liam_dev: starting a bisect now on a small smoke set (50 pairs) — will report back.

evalbot: schedule | smoke-bisect started by liam_dev | target-range=5f4e7..a1b2c3d | runner=ci/smoke-bisect | timestamp=3623456796

mina: also can we add a deterministic tokenization check to our eval harness? i.e., compare token id sequences across model builds before scoring. would catch these shifts earlier.

chen_w: yes — add `--token-check` flag that writes token sequences and diffs them. we should fail the rollout if >0.1% token divergence for locale-specific datasets.

liam_dev: bisect result: culprit commit = a189f7e (fast-kv: pack-merger optimization). reverting that patch removes the duplicate id.

mina: thanks. file a revert PR? also want a test preventing this for vertical/furigana cases. I'll draft a small dataset of edge cases (ruby, zwj, narrow no-break spaces).

chen_w: i'll own the PR to add the `--token-check` flag in the harness. assigning to @chen_w :thumbsup:

mina: created issue #4127 with sample artifacts and outputs. linking logs: https://redwood-internal/issue/4127

liam_dev: follow-up — we should also test on other locales with diacritics + RTL to ensure merge logic is robust; adding Arabic+Hebrew smoke tests to the suite.

mina: agreed. i'll add zh-ja-ruby and ar-he-rtl sets to nightly regression matrix. thanks everyone. :pray:

evalbot: nightly-run scheduled to include updated smoke tests after PR merge.
